clue.text: Steps down, blocked by editor's new plans

indicators.note: the first word is obstructed by the second, which is put inside it

parts.note: someone who steps down from a post resigns
ED is the standard short form of editor; the 's is part of the word

explanation.surface: A newspaper story: the people stepping down are thwarted by an editor's fresh scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps down' reads as the definition at the start, but the definition is at the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb taking a third-person subject: drawing up fresh plans for something is exactly what redrafting its layout means.

clue.text: Go over requirement for cardinal, having skipped first of duties

indicators.note: skipping something means leaving it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a Roman Catholic cardinal wears a scarlet hat, a red cap

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A churchman reviews what a cardinal needs, having ignored the first of his duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having skipped' removes D, the first letter that 'first of' takes from 'duties', from REDCAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to go over again means to summarise, the short form of recapitulate.

clue.text: French navy possibly supporting party initially under leader at Waterloo?

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the one it holds up

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party or celebration

indicators.note: initially means take the word's opening letter

parts.note: bleu is French for blue, and navy is one shade of it

explanation.surface: Musing on a French fleet backing a party under Wellington's or Napoleon's command at Waterloo.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'leader at Waterloo' is the first letter of that word, W, whose name in full is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter heading the word Waterloo is W, and spelt out as a name that letter is written out this way.

clue.text: Tower to lease, in coastal area around South

indicators.note: in places the leasing word within the rest
the coastal area goes around, so it contains the next letter

parts.note: the shore is the land along the sea's edge
to lease something is to hire it

explanation.surface: An estate agent's listing: a tower for rent in a seaside district facing south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower' is one who tows, not a tall building; the South letter goes inside the coastal word before the leasing word goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy draught breed of horse was used for pulling loads, so it is one that tows.

clue.text: One's cut up after French cut down in wartime arena

indicators.note: after places the first piece of the clue later in the answer
cut down means shortened, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: Gallic means French, from Gaul

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: Battle imagery: a soldier is wounded after French forces are slaughtered somewhere in the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the one-plus-cut piece to read POLI; 'after' puts it behind the shortened French word.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1915-16 campaign on this Turkish peninsula made it a famous First World War battleground.

clue.text: Collection of items go to court — one item in particular involved

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action in court
the pronoun it refers to one particular thing

explanation.surface: A legal dispute over a collection where one specific piece is at issue.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching set of things, such as furniture or rooms, is called by this word.

clue.text: Experts bagging money for peak achievements

indicators.note: bagging means putting into a bag, so it holds the next piece

parts.note: aces are people who excel at something

explanation.surface: Top professionals pocketing cash for their finest results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bagging' puts M inside ACES.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: each summit or highest point reached is an acme, plural here.

clue.text: Current measures so far blocked by politician

indicators.note: blocked by means obstructed from inside, so the second piece goes within

parts.note: as far as and so far as are interchangeable, so here as stands for so far
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Present policies have up to now been obstructed by a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' is electrical flow, not 'present'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere is the unit measuring electrical flow, so these are units of it.

clue.text: Chaos in a city on Sicily

parts.note: a mess is a state of disorder

explanation.surface: Disorder in some city on the Italian island.
explanation.definitionFit: The port on the Sicilian strait facing mainland Italy bears this name.

clue.text: Jewish traditionalists mention cut in religious areas

indicators.note: in places the second piece inside the first

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

indicators.note: cut means shortened, losing the final letter

parts.note: to adduce is to cite or mention as evidence

explanation.surface: Orthodox believers refer to a reduction in church territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'religious areas' are bishops' dioceses, not churches or temples.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient Jewish sect held strictly to the written Law, rejecting later oral teaching.

clue.text: Key point that's missed by vineyard

indicators.note: the letter X, a cross, is the one missed out, so the word loses it

parts.note: the crux is the central point of a matter

explanation.surface: An important feature that a vineyard overlooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's missed' removes X from CRUX.
explanation.definitionFit: French wine term for a vineyard or growth of a recognised quality, as in grand cru.

clue.text: Unpleasant odd ellipsis, out of place

indicators.note: letters that are out of place need rearranging

explanation.surface: A grumble that a strange set of three dots is misplaced and nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' looks like the adjective but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being hostile or unfriendly in attitude is close to being disagreeable.

clue.text: Ground turned up, delivers rocks

indicators.note: turned means the following word is turned round
rocks as a verb means shakes, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Earth disturbed and brought to the surface as stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes PU from UP; 'rocks' rearranges DELIVERS to LVERISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense synonym: to crush into powder is to grind it.

clue.text: Story linked to university place at the Sorbonne

parts.note: a story can be a falsehood, a lie

explanation.surface: A tale tied to a Paris university.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sorbonne is a Paris university, so the definition asks for French.
explanation.definitionFit: French word for place, also used in English in 'in lieu of'.

clue.text: Collaborative worker, one occupying no permanent level?

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside, so this piece goes within the others

parts.note: temp describes something temporary, the opposite of permanent
a means one
a layer is a level or stratum

explanation.surface: A cooperative worker holding a non-permanent rung of the hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' puts A inside TEMPLAYER, after TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone who works well with colleagues is described this way.

clue.text: Funny dog pound in position beside rear of zoo

indicators.note: beside means placed next to, joining the pieces
in places the next piece inside the first

parts.note: to put is to position something
L is the abbreviation for the pound sterling

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A comic dog put in the pound next to the back of the zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' is the money, not an animal shelter; 'in' puts L inside PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mickey Mouse's comic pet in Disney cartoons, a cartoon animal.

clue.text: Help out with stamp booklets

indicators.note: out means not in proper order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An instruction to lend a hand with postage on some little books.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: slim unbound publications on a single topic are small booklets.

clue.text: Love those people in nude, mostly looking for sex?

parts.note: love means zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: in places the people inside the trimmed word
mostly means nearly all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: naked means nude
them refers to those people

explanation.surface: A cheeky scene: someone after sex, keen on unclothed people.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'those people' piece goes in after the first letter of the shortened nude word.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: chasing a sexual conquest (or profit) is described by this phrase; the question mark marks one sense.

clue.text: Gossip, say, indicating length in lace-worker's outputs

indicators.note: in places the length abbreviation within the other piece

parts.note: tatting is a handmade lace, so a lacemaker produces tattings

explanation.surface: Chatter, perhaps, about the size of a lacemaker's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' shows the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle chattering talk about others is this kind of tittle-tattle.

clue.text: Right to avoid outlet stocking dodgy fish — it's not likely to last

indicators.note: stocking means holding goods in stock, so this goes around the next piece
to avoid means a letter is left out

parts.note: a market is a sales outlet

indicators.note: dodgy means suspect, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A shop advised not to sell off fish, which won't stay fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' turns the fish into SHIF, which the shortened outlet word holds after its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something improvised as a temporary stopgap is unlikely to endure.

clue.text: A lot of hot air from bad actors in family

indicators.note: in places the actors inside the family word

parts.note: kin means family
hams are overacting performers

explanation.surface: A family of terrible performers producing nothing but bluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot air' looks like empty talk but is literal wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot dry dust-laden wind blowing in Egypt and North Africa in spring.

clue.text: Whales knocking out new sound detectors

indicators.note: knocking out means removing a letter from the word

parts.note: minkes are a species of small whale

explanation.surface: Whales disabling some fresh hydrophones.
explanation.definitionFit: Short informal word for microphones, which pick up sound.

clue.text: European country picked up delay linked to one from Arab country

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, reading upwards

parts.note: UK stands for the United Kingdom
to wait is to delay
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A European nation's postponement tied to a person from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' makes KU from UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective: belonging to the Gulf state of Kuwait.

clue.text: Dodgy car costing little, front coming off

indicators.note: losing the front means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: cheap means inexpensive

explanation.surface: A cheap old banger whose bumper falls off.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a dilapidated old car, an old banger.

clue.text: Someone unwanted at dance? Women — every female — scowl

parts.note: all means every
to lower (rhymes with flower) is to frown or scowl

explanation.surface: At a dance the ladies all glower at someone they don't want.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a person left without a partner at a dance, sitting by the wall.

clue.text: Warning signal sees children leaving room

indicators.note: leaving means taking these letters out

parts.note: a chamber is a room
CH is an abbreviation for child or children

explanation.surface: A warning that children are leaving the room.
explanation.definitionFit: The traffic light colour between green and red warns drivers to stop.

clue.text: Send last component of 29 up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading the word upwards

parts.note: 29's clue ends with the word part-timer, whose last part is timer

explanation.surface: Instruction to send something up.
explanation.walkthrough: '29' refers to the clue at 29 across, which ends 'part-timer'; 'up' reverses TIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to remit is to dispatch money or a document.

clue.text: Royal fighter intervening in tax enactment

indicators.note: intervening in means coming between, so the word sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A regal warrior meddles in passing a tax law.
explanation.definitionFit: The TV heroine of 'Xena: Warrior Princess' is a royal combatant.

clue.text: Children's character unknown to feisty urban teens

indicators.note: feisty means lively, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A kids' character is a mystery to some spirited city adolescents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feisty' rearranges URBAN TEENS to EASTERBUNN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit figure who brings chocolate eggs to children at Easter.

clue.text: Member following one's guiding principle

indicators.note: following means the member goes after

parts.note: I's is one's, I being one

explanation.surface: An MP sticking to their own guiding doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a distinctive doctrine or belief system, like socialism.

clue.text: Commercialised version of saint, note, put forward by devilish figure

indicators.note: put forward means moved nearer the front of the word

parts.note: Satan is the devil

explanation.surface: A shopping-mall Nicholas pushed forward by a demonic figure.
explanation.walkthrough: N moves from the end of SATAN to its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas descends from Saint Nicholas, now a figure of seasonal shopping.

clue.text: Soldiers turned against coming in to oppose part-timer

indicators.note: coming in to means entering, so the soldiers go within

parts.note: to resist is to oppose

indicators.note: turned means the soldiers' letters face the other way

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
V is the abbreviation for versus, against

explanation.surface: Troops turn against joining in to resist a part-time member.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps; the soldiers-plus-against piece enters after the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve soldier trains part-time alongside civilian work.
